output.summary: Deploy a secure, high-performance static website for csce412advaithr07.me using a private S3 origin, CloudFront CDN with OAC, an ACM TLS certificate, and Route 53 DNS routing.
requirements: Host five static website pages and a custom 404.html page in a private S3 bucket with all public access blocked.
Deliver content via a CloudFront distribution utilizing Origin Access Control (OAC) to strictly forbid anonymous S3 access.
Provision a public ACM TLS certificate in us-east-1 covering csce412advaithr07.me.
Enforce viewer protocol policy to redirect HTTP requests to HTTPS.
Configure custom error response on CloudFront to serve custom 404.html on HTTP 404 status.
Configure Route 53 DNS alias records pointing csce412advaithr07.me to the CloudFront distribution.
service_dependencies: S3: Stores static website files (five pages + 404 page) in a private bucket with public access blocked, accessible only by CloudFront via bucket policy.

CloudFront: Acts as the CDN distribution serving content globally, enforcing HTTPS redirection, attaching the ACM certificate, applying OAC for S3 origin, and routing 404 errors to the custom error page.
ACM: Provisions and validates the public SSL/TLS certificate in us-east-1 for csce412advaithr07.me to enable HTTPS delivery.
Route 53: Manages DNS records for csce412advaithr07.me, validating ACM certificate via DNS CNAME records and routing apex domain traffic to CloudFront via Alias A record.
risks: Requesting the ACM certificate in a region other than us-east-1, preventing CloudFront from associating with it.
Misconfigured S3 bucket policy or OAC leading to HTTP 403 Forbidden errors or unintended public access.
DNS propagation delays or missing Route 53 hosted zone delegation at the domain registrar delaying certificate issuance and site resolution.
Custom 404 error response caching or returning incorrect HTTP response codes (e.g., returning 200 OK instead of 404).

tasks.action: Create Route 53 public hosted zone for csce412advaithr07.me if not already present.
Request a public ACM TLS certificate for csce412advaithr07.me in the us-east-1 region using DNS validation.
Create Route 53 CNAME validation records generated by ACM for csce412advaithr07.me.
Verify that the ACM certificate in us-east-1 has successfully transitioned to ISSUED status.
Create an S3 bucket with all Public Access Block settings enabled and default server-side encryption.
Upload five static site HTML pages and the custom 404.html error page to the S3 bucket.
Create CloudFront distribution with S3 origin, OAC, viewer protocol redirect-to-https, ACM certificate, default root object index.html, and custom 404 error response.
Attach S3 bucket policy permitting s3:GetObject solely to the CloudFront distribution service principal using the created OAC.
Create Route 53 A and AAAA Alias records mapping csce412advaithr07.me to the CloudFront distribution domain name.
Validate DNS resolution, HTTPS certificate validity, HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect, custom 404 handling, and verify direct S3 access is blocked.

questions: Is the domain csce412advaithr07.me registered directly with Route 53, or is it registered with an external registrar requiring name server delegation?
Should the deployment also support the 'www' subdomain (e.g., www.csce412advaithr07.me) with a redirect to the apex domain?
Should the custom 404 error response retain the HTTP 404 status code or return HTTP 200 for single-page application routing?
